note: Wall-pilot rules of the fast race-cue pilot inside the obstacle stack (visual_brain --obstacle-stack on|shadow; off by default and outside the stack; --wall-pilot off removes them from the stack). 'turn_first': haltere.liftoff.fast_race_cue.TurnFirstConfig, turn before translating at a wall the drone cannot stop before when the next checkpoint is far off the heading or its marker is lost (a hairpin), with its stopping model per motor contract in 'turn_first_stopping'. 'ceiling_guard': haltere.liftoff.fast_race_cue.CeilingGuardConfig, keep the looming TTC governor's terrain climb out of ceilings and overhangs (unchanged from version 3). Generic and course-agnostic: they read only the pilot's own state, the causal looming samples, odometry and the visible checkpoint marker; the stopping model is a measured motor property, not a course value. Version 4 was designed after inspecting the round-3 Minus Two logs it addresses (minus-brain09b-vg-01, minus-brain08-vg-01, minus-fast6-vg-02) and earlier logs (minus-fast6-gapon-01), so those replays are development evidence, not held-out evidence. It was frozen with its offline gates (configs/obstacles/wall_pilot_gates.json) before any replay of version 4. The runner refuses another version (fast_race_cue.WALL_PILOT_VERSION). The hash covers everything except frozen/frozen_at/sha256; a change needs a new version and a new freeze before any live flight, and every version flown is reported. Offline replays of these rules are open loop and are not flight evidence. Version 5 adds 'clearance_brake' (haltere.liftoff.fast_race_cue.ClearanceBrakeConfig): the TTC governor's clearance brake never commands a descent the pilot did not ask for.

turn_first_notes.condition: near a wall, at a measured horizontal speed of at most max_speed (the task's ~3.5 m/s: the low-speed hairpin regime; above it the governor's own cap acts alone): either the TTC governor holds a stand-off (a wall sample capped the request at standoff_speed, 2 m/s, or less within standoff_s) with the latest wall sample within the stopping distance from max(closing speed, standoff_speed), or its wall brake capped the request within brake_recent_s and the latest wall sample lies within the stopping distance at the closing speed. The latest wall sample is the newest looming sample the governor did not brake for as terrain with an aged TTC below hold_ttc_s (1.3 s); its remaining distance is its capture-time reach along its looming ray minus the odometry travelled along that ray since, 0 once reached or passed (e.g. a gate arch flown through). Stopping distance: v*stop_latency_s + v^2/(2*stop_deceleration) + stop_margin_m, v the measured velocity along that ray (>= 0). And the checkpoint: its marker clamped at a side edge or corner (pilot state side), its filtered bearing (in view, or clamped at the bottom/top edge away from the corners) engage_deg or more off the heading, or its marker lost (pilot state coast: seen more than 0.25 s ago, the pilot repeats its last request)
turn_first_notes.action: the horizontal request loses its component toward the wall (the horizontal part of the looming ray that capped the request, taken at engagement) and is bounded to creep_speed, or to coast_creep_speed (0: hold) while the marker is lost, since the direction to creep toward is not known; the request's speed toward the wall is removed, and its horizontal speed brought to that bound, at the clearance brake_slew (15 m/s^2, beyond the usual 0.25 s taper); the vertical request and the yaw rule are unchanged, so the assisted yaw keeps turning toward the checkpoint
turn_first_notes.release: aligned: the bearing of a marker in view (or bottom/top clamped) is within release_deg of the heading (the ordinary speed schedule and acceleration limits then resume); handoff: search, launch or a support climb owns the request; timeout: max_s after engagement, then no new episode for rearm_s, so the drone never hovers at a wall indefinitely
turn_first_notes.side_guard: during that rearm time, in pilot state side while the wall condition holds, the side rule's request still loses its component toward the wall (the governor's current wall ray), without the creep bound: the side rule never pushes along a wall it is near (minus-fast6-gapon-01)
turn_first_notes.max_speed: 3.5 m/s: the task's engagement range (governor caps and speeds up to ~3.5 m/s). Above it the stopping distance at race speed exceeds every looming alarm distance, so the distance test would no longer discriminate, and an episode would be a hard stop at race speed
turn_first_notes.coast_creep_speed: 0 m/s: with the marker lost the checkpoint direction is unknown; the stale lateral part of the last request can point toward the wall when the wall ray (the old travel direction) is not the wall normal

turn_first_stopping_notes.fast_velocity_brain_v1: brain-09b (fast-brain-09b-caps-r0001m100, the braking brain candidate), measured on minus-brain09b-vg-01: request drops of >= 1 m/s at 11.96, 17.93 and 20.67 s gave a delay to the speed drop of 0.32 / 0.19 / 0.26 s and a deceleration over the next 0.3 s of 3.64 / 3.70 / 3.88 m/s^2 (scratchpad m4/hairpin braking.py; same method for every motor): declared 0.3 s and 3.5 m/s^2. brain-08 shares the contract but does not brake for such requests (delay 0.3-1.0 s, deceleration about 0 on minus-brain08-vg-01, -gapon-01/02, -loom-01): for it this model is optimistic
turn_first_stopping_notes.fast_velocity_pd_v1: fast PD, measured on minus-fast6-vg-02, minus-fast6-gapon-01, minus-fast6-wall-01 and pine-fast6-ttc-01 (12 request drops): delay 0.11-0.19 s (median 0.13), deceleration over 0.3 s 4.2-10.4 m/s^2 (median about 6.5): declared 0.15 s and 6 m/s^2
turn_first_stopping_notes.default: the brain contract's model (the slower braking) for any other motor

ceiling_guard_notes.unexplained_alarms: without the guard a sample without vertical evidence (below_fraction None: one of looming2's vertical windows has no evidence, or neither is urgent) counts as terrain while a climb is active. On minus-brain08-gapon-01 the alarms from the garage ceiling ahead of the climbing path (TTC 0.93 -> 0.43 s, below_fraction None, lower TTC none or 1.23 s) raised the climb from 0.4 to 3.5 m/s. With the guard such a sample is terrain only when the lower window explains it (lower TTC <= lower_ratio x alarm TTC), otherwise a wall
ceiling_guard_notes.weak_climb: a climb from such an explained sample (terrain seen by the lower window only) requests at most weak_climb (the task's ~1 m/s), refreshes the climb hold only at that level, and is ignored weak_climb_max_m above where the last below-path climb request (below_fraction >= terrain_fraction) was accepted; below-path climbs keep the TTC policy's vertical_up and climb_max_m
ceiling_guard_notes.overhead: during a climb (or an overhead hold), while the measured vertical speed exceeds overhead_min_rise, a sample with alarm TTC < overhead_ttc_s (the TTC policy's climb_on_s) whose expansion lies above the path (below_fraction <= overhead_fraction) or is unexplained is overhead evidence; overhead_confirm of them within the governor's confirm_window_s (0.25 s), at least overhead_positive of them positive (see overhead_positive), cut the climb to 0 and start an overhead hold of hold_s, renewed by further confirmed evidence: no terrain climb, below-path samples brake like walls (terrain_brake 0 would otherwise let rising ground pass unbraked), and the whole vertical request (pilot and governor) is bounded to vertical_cap (level) and brought down at vertical_slew m/s^2 (the clearance brake_slew) instead of the pilot's 5 m/s^2. Level flight is unaffected: overhead evidence only counts during a climb or a hold, and only while the drone rises
ceiling_guard_notes.not_used: looming2 already fits an 'up' window 0.12 W above the focus of expansion (ttc_upper, report only). It is not published by the camera process and the live logs do not carry it; while climbing, that window lies at the top of the image, where the HUD mask removes the upper 20 % (on gapon-01 at 18.5 s the lower window was urgent while below_fraction was None, so the upper window had no evidence under the ceiling). The guard therefore uses the fields the camera already publishes
ceiling_guard_notes.overhead_min_rise: a ceiling or overhang can only cross a rising flight path; an alarm ahead of a level or sinking path is braked for as a wall and does not stop a climb that arrests a sink. 0.3 m/s is a noise margin on the measured vertical speed, not fitted
ceiling_guard_notes.overhead_positive: a sample is positive overhead evidence when something shows that the alarm is not the surface below the path: below_fraction <= overhead_fraction (the expansion lies above the path), or a lower-surface TTC that is known and longer than lower_ratio x the alarm TTC. A sample in which neither vertical window crosses the path (below_fraction None and lower TTC None) says nothing either way: climbing a hill, both windows often lose it. Such samples still count toward overhead_confirm but cannot confirm alone. On gapon-02 the confirming sample had below_fraction 0.0; on gapon-01 the ceiling alarms included a lower TTC of 1.23 s against an alarm of 0.63 s

clearance_brake_notes.rule: the TTC wall cap bounds the request's component along the looming ray (the travel direction at the sample's capture): the brake subtracts ray x (along - cap) from the request, and _cap_command brings the command's component along the ray to the cap at brake_slew. After each of the two steps the vertical request (command) is at least min(its value before the step, 0) - max_added_sink (0 m/s): the brake may reduce a climb to level and may raise the request when the ray points down, but it adds no sink. Its horizontal part is unchanged; the vertical guard's and the pilot's own sink are untouched. Applied only with the stack on (wall_apply); in shadow it is measured and logged, not applied
clearance_brake_notes.why: round-4 live flight minus-fast6-r4-02 (development case, found by the round-4b guard agent): from 26.4 s the stand-off cap (0.53-0.62 m/s) along a travel ray tilted about 11 deg up ((-0.80, 0.58, 0.19)), renewed by wall samples until 29.7 s, turned the pilot's and guard's +0.1..+0.23 m/s into a command of -0.3..-0.5 m/s: the drone skimmed the garage floor (z < 0.1 m for 1.5 s at 27.4-28.9 s). The sink request below -0.3 m/s also fed the descent-path governor (horizontal cut to its floor) and would have fed the support rules
clearance_brake_notes.alternatives: correcting only the horizontal part (the ray's horizontal projection, scaled so the 3-D component meets the cap) brakes harder horizontally on every rising ray and changes the brake on every Minus log; the floor at min(request, 0) keeps the horizontal part bit for bit and changes only the vertical request on ticks where the brake added sink. Chosen before any replay of version 5
clearance_brake_notes.evidence: development only: the open-loop replay of minus-fast6-r4-02 (the case that motivated the rule) was looked at before the freeze; the gates (configs/obstacles/wall_pilot_gates.json version 2) are frozen with this version, before any replay of it is scored

change: v5 (round 4b, after the round-4 live flights): the clearance brake's sink floor only (clearance_brake). Turn-first, its stopping models and the ceiling guard are version 4's values, unchanged.
